title: Anchor OOM staleness to the latest memory sample
answers: Why did VPA discard a recent OOM as too old?
Why was the expected memory bump missing after an OOM near an aggregation boundary?
What timestamp should RecordOOM use to decide whether an OOM is stale?
body:
Symptom: VPA discards a recent OOM as "too old" near a memory aggregation boundary, preventing the expected memory bump-up.
Root cause: vertical-pod-autoscaler/pkg/recommender/model/container.go:ContainerState.RecordOOM used WindowEnd as its staleness reference; usage samples advance that boundary up to a full interval ahead of the latest real sample.
Fix pattern: Compare event age against lastMemorySampleStart, the latest observed memory sample, and skip the staleness check when that reference is zero.
Constraints: Preserve the single aggregation interval cutoff: reject timestamps strictly before lastMemorySampleStart minus GetMemoryAggregationIntervalDuration(). Do not substitute WindowEnd, wall-clock time, or the full interval-times-count window.
applies: VPA recommender OOM recording and changes to memory aggregation or event staleness handling.
